model: TEC26x7-4 and TEC26x7-4+PIR Thermostat with Two Outputs (BACnet MS/TP)
applies_to: Hydronic reheat valves, pressure-dependent VAV boxes with or without reheat and other zoning equipment, using the two-output TEC26x7-4 thermostats (TEC2627 on/off or floating, TEC2647 proportional).
summary: The TEC26x7-4 thermostats control zoning equipment with two outputs over BACnet MS/TP. The list covers system mode, occupancy command, six setpoints, loop demands, valve status, input status, alarms and configuration. There is no fan mode or fan status object; the valve timing objects apply to the TEC2627.
notes: Objects from Table 5 on pages 22-25 of the technical bulletin, which also holds separate tables for the other TEC26xx-4 models.
Access comes from the guide's footnotes: read/write, read-only, or writable only after the matching override object is set to Override.
The device object (instance 72aaa, aaa = MS/TP address) is not listed as a point.
Temperatures are listed in °F; the guide also gives the °C range.

source.title: TEC Series BACnet MS/TP Network Temperature and Humidity Controllers Technical Bulletin

integration.summary: Address the thermostat on the BACnet MS/TP trunk, then command System Mode (MV 16) and Occupancy Command (MV 18) and write the occupied setpoints (AV 39/40). Read Room Temp, Effective Occupancy, the PI demands and the filter and service alarms.

minimum_points.name: System Mode
minimum_points.why: System mode: off, auto, cool or heat

integration.enable: Occupancy Command (MV 18, 1=Resume Schedule, 2=Occupied, 3=Unoccupied, 4=Temporary Occupied) sets occupancy from the BAS; the first state hands occupancy back to the thermostat. System Mode (MV 16) can switch the unit off.
integration.heartbeat: The guide marks some objects (Room Temp) as possibly releasing on their own after 10 minutes with no BACnet traffic. Keep writing overridden values.
integration.remote_sensors: To feed room temperature from the BAS, set Room Temp Override (BV 8) to Override, then write Room Temp (AV 7). Outdoor Temperature (AV 9) is only valid when it is written over the network.
setup: BACnet MS/TP only. Set the MS/TP address (4 to 127) with the Com addr parameter at the thermostat.
The thermostat names itself TEC26x7-aaa and picks device instance 72aaa, where aaa is the MS/TP address (e.g. 72004). Change either before mapping points if needed.
Leave the thermostat on automatic baud detection; at least one device on the trunk (normally the supervisory controller) needs a fixed baud rate.
Max_Master in the device object is writable.
gotchas: Writing one setpoint of a heating/cooling pair can make the thermostat move the other one to keep the minimum deadband.
Set the configuration parameters before mapping; the guide recommends re-mapping all objects if configuration changes afterwards.
TEC26xx-4 objects do not line up with the older TEC26xx-2 objects; rediscover all points when replacing a -2 thermostat.
Objects with no access mark in the guide are listed here as read-only.
